reading.body:
CyrusOne's Austin AUS2-AUS3 campus publishes 19 MW of IT load capacity across 242,000 square feet, a scale that constrains AI training but matches its compliance certifications for regulated workloads.

The 19 MW figure is the published ceiling for compute at this site. Across 242,000 square feet of technical space, that is an average of about 79 watts per square foot. The data does not state whether power delivery can exceed this average for individual racks.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, point to regulated workloads in financial services, healthcare, and federal use. The suitability score of 62 is based only on published IT capacity and operator type, and it lists no announced expansion. This means the score does not capture whether the site can absorb new GPU demand beyond its current published load.

What the data does not show is actual availability, grid interconnection quality, or power delivery headroom. The 19 MW is a ceiling, not a confirmed usable capacity for high-density AI training. A reader evaluating this campus for AI compute should treat the published IT load as the upper bound and seek additional power and expansion data before assuming it can host material GPU infrastructure.
